name: Beeri
overview: Beeri is a male figure in Scripture known primarily as the father of the prophet Hosea. The biblical text does not specify his tribe or provide additional personal details beyond this familial connection. His mention is concise, serving mainly to identify Hosea's lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Beeri means '[my] cistern, well' in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name without indication of divine origin. This meaning suggests a source or reservoir, though the text does not elaborate on its significance for Beeri personally.
familyAndRelationships: Beeri is identified as the father of Hosea, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Scripture does not record any other family connections for Beeri beyond this role.
scriptureSignificance: Beeri's significance in the biblical narrative rests chiefly on his role as the father of Hosea, one of the twelve minor prophets. This connection situates him within the prophetic tradition and provides a genealogical anchor for Hosea's ministry. Although Beeri himself does not appear prominently in the storyline, his mention underscores the human lineage through which God's prophetic message was communicated.
